title: Direct & Indirect Speech
subtitle: SSC CGL Tier 1 + Tier 2 Complete Notes

definition.english: Narration is the way in which the words spoken by one person are reported to another person. It has two forms: Direct Speech and Indirect Speech.
definition.marathi: एका व्यक्तीने बोललेले वाक्य दुसऱ्या व्यक्तीला सांगण्याच्या पद्धतीला Narration (Direct & Indirect Speech) म्हणतात.

examples.word: Ram said that he was busy.

types.name: Direct Speech
types.english: The speaker's exact words are written as they are, within quotation marks (" ").
types.marathi: Speaker चे शब्द जसेच्या तसे (" ") मध्ये लिहिले जातात.
examples: Ram said, "I am busy."

types.name: Indirect Speech
types.english: The speaker's words are reported in one's own language, without quotation marks.
types.marathi: Speaker चे शब्द आपल्या भाषेत सांगितले जातात.
examples: Ram said that he was busy.

goldenConcept.title: SSC Golden Concept: Reporting Verb Tense Rule
goldenConcept.english: Whether the tense changes in Indirect Speech depends entirely on the tense of the Reporting Verb, not just on habit.
goldenConcept.marathi: Reported Speech मधील Tense Change हे केवळ सवयीने नाही तर Reporting Verb च्या Tense वर अवलंबून असते.
wrongThinking: Indirect Speech मध्ये Tense नेहमीच बदलतो
Reporting Verb कडे लक्ष न देता थेट Tense बदलणे
correctThinking: Reporting Verb Present/Future/Present Perfect असल्यास -> Tense Change होत नाही
Reporting Verb Past असल्यास -> Tense Change होतो

rules.title: Narration म्हणजे काय
rules.english: Narration is the way of reporting what one person has said to another person.
rules.marathi: एका व्यक्तीने बोललेले वाक्य दुसऱ्या व्यक्तीला सांगण्याच्या पद्धतीला Narration म्हणतात.
examples: Ram said, "I am busy."
Ram said that he was busy.

rules.title: Direct Speech चे दोन भाग - Reporting Verb
rules.english: Reporting Verb is the verb used by the person who reported the sentence.
rules.marathi: ज्याने वाक्य सांगितले त्या Verb ला Reporting Verb म्हणतात.
examples: Ram said, "I am busy." (said = Reporting Verb)

rules.title: Direct Speech चे दोन भाग - Reported Speech
rules.english: Reported Speech is the actual sentence that was spoken, written inside quotation marks.
rules.marathi: जे प्रत्यक्ष बोलले गेले तो भाग म्हणजे Reported Speech.
examples: Ram said, "I am busy." ("I am busy." = Reported Speech)

rules.title: Reporting Verb Present/Future/Present Perfect - No Tense Change
rules.english: If the Reporting Verb is in Present, Future or Present Perfect, the tense of Reported Speech does not change.
rules.marathi: Reporting Verb Present/Future/Present Perfect मध्ये असेल तर Tense Change होत नाही.
examples: He says, "I work hard." → He says that he works hard.

rules.title: Reporting Verb Past - Tense Change
rules.english: If the Reporting Verb is in Past tense, the tense of Reported Speech changes accordingly.
rules.marathi: Reporting Verb Past मध्ये असेल तर Tense Change होतो.
examples: He said, "I work hard." → He said that he worked hard.

wrongRight.wrong: He said that I am busy.
wrongRight.right: He said that I was busy.

rules.title: Tense Change होत नाही अशी परिस्थिती
rules.english: Tense does not change when the Reporting Verb is Present/Future, or the sentence expresses a universal truth, scientific fact, habitual fact, historical fact, or when Reported Speech is already in Past Perfect / Past Perfect Continuous.
rules.marathi: Reporting Verb Present/Future, Universal Truth, Scientific Fact, Habitual Fact, Historical Fact किंवा Reported Speech आधीच Past Perfect/Past Perfect Continuous मध्ये असेल तर Tense Change होत नाही.
examples: The teacher said, "The Sun rises in the East." → The teacher said that the Sun rises in the East.
He says, "I am ready." → He says that he is ready.

rules.title: Pronoun Change Rule
rules.english: While changing pronouns, consider the Speaker, the Listener, and any Third Person mentioned.
rules.marathi: Pronoun बदलताना Speaker, Listener आणि Third Person यांचा विचार करावा.
examples: Ram said, "I am happy." → Ram said that he was happy.
Ram said to Mohan, "You are lazy." → Ram told Mohan that he was lazy.

rules.title: Statement Sentence - Said + That
rules.english: For Assertive/Statement sentences, use Said + That before the reported clause.
rules.marathi: Statement Sentence साठी Said + That वापरतात.
examples: He said, "I am ready." → He said that he was ready.

rules.title: Said To → Told Rule
rules.english: When the Reporting Verb is 'said to' followed by a person, it changes to 'told'.
rules.marathi: Reporting Verb 'said to' नंतर व्यक्ती असल्यास तो 'told' मध्ये बदलतो.
examples: Ram said to Mohan, "I am busy." → Ram told Mohan that he was busy.

wrongRight.wrong: He said to me that he was ready.
wrongRight.right: He told me that he was ready.

rules.title: Assertive Sentence Structure
rules.english: Assertive sentence structure in Indirect Speech: Subject + Said/Told + That + Sentence.
rules.marathi: Assertive Sentence ची रचना: Subject + Said/Told + That + Sentence.
examples: He said that he was ready.

rules.title: Interrogative Sentence - Yes/No Question
rules.english: For Yes/No questions, the Reporting Verb changes to Asked/Inquired/Wanted to know, and If/Whether connects the clause.
rules.marathi: Yes/No Question साठी Reporting Verb Asked/Inquired/Wanted to know होतो आणि If/Whether ने clause जोडतात.
examples: He said, "Are you ready?" → He asked if I was ready.

rules.title: Interrogative Sentence - WH Question
rules.english: For WH questions (Why, What, Who, Where, When, Which, Whose, How), the WH word remains unchanged and the Reporting Verb becomes Asked.
rules.marathi: WH Question मध्ये Why, What, Who, Where, When, Which, Whose, How हे शब्द तसेच राहतात आणि Reporting Verb Asked होतो.
examples: He said, "Where are you going?" → He asked where I was going.

wrongRight.wrong: He asked that where I was going.
wrongRight.right: He asked where I was going.

rules.title: Imperative Sentence Rule
rules.english: For Imperative sentences, the Reporting Verb becomes Ordered/Requested/Advised/Warned/Commanded/Urged/Begged/Told, and V1 changes to To + V1.
rules.marathi: Imperative Sentence साठी Reporting Verb Ordered/Requested/Advised/Warned/Commanded/Urged/Begged/Told होतो आणि V1 चा To + V1 होतो.
examples: Teacher said, "Work hard." → Teacher advised us to work hard.
Mother said, "Open the door." → Mother told me to open the door.

rules.title: Negative Imperative - Not To + V1
rules.english: In negative commands, Don't + V1 changes to Not to + V1.
rules.marathi: Negative Imperative मध्ये Don't + V1 चा Not to + V1 होतो.
examples: Mother said, "Don't waste time." → Mother advised me not to waste time.

wrongRight.wrong: Mother advised me don't waste time.
wrongRight.right: Mother advised me not to waste time.

rules.title: Exclamatory Sentence Rule
rules.english: For Exclamatory sentences, the Reporting Verb changes to Exclaimed with joy/sorrow/surprise/wonder/regret depending on the emotion.
rules.marathi: Exclamatory Sentence साठी भावनेनुसार Reporting Verb Exclaimed with joy/sorrow/surprise/wonder/regret होतो.
examples: He said, "Hurrah! We won." → He exclaimed with joy that they had won.

rules.title: Optative Sentence Rule
rules.english: For Optative sentences expressing a wish, blessing or prayer, the Reporting Verb becomes Prayed/Wished/Blessed/Cursed.
rules.marathi: Optative Sentence साठी Reporting Verb Prayed/Wished/Blessed/Cursed होतो.
examples: He said, "May God bless you." → He prayed that God might bless me.

rules.title: Modal Changes
rules.english: Modals change as follows: Will→Would, Shall→Should/Would, Can→Could, May→Might, Must→Had to (context nusar Must can remain unchanged).
rules.marathi: Will→Would, Shall→Should/Would, Can→Could, May→Might, Must→Had to (Context नुसार Must तसाच राहू शकतो).
examples: He said, "I will come." → He said that he would come.

wrongRight.wrong: He said that he will come.
wrongRight.right: He said that he would come.

pyqTraps.wrong: He said that I am busy.
pyqTraps.right: He said that I was busy.

pyqTraps.wrong: He said that he will come.
pyqTraps.right: He said that he would come.

pyqTraps.wrong: He asked that where I was going.
pyqTraps.right: He asked where I was going.

pyqTraps.wrong: He said to me that he was ready.
pyqTraps.right: He told me that he was ready.

pyqTraps.wrong: Mother advised me don't waste time.
pyqTraps.right: Mother advised me not to waste time.

examStrategy.english: Focus on the basic Tense Change table, Said→That, Said to→Told, Pronoun Change, and the Present/Past Reporting Verb rule, since these are asked most frequently.
examStrategy.marathi: मुख्यतः Tense Change Table, Said→That, Said to→Told, Pronoun Change आणि Present/Past Reporting Verb Rule वर लक्ष द्या, हे सर्वाधिक वेळा विचारले जातात.

examStrategy.english: Revise Yes/No and WH Questions, Imperative and Negative Imperative, Exclamatory, Optative sentences, Modal Changes, and the No-Tense-Change exceptions (universal truth, scientific/historical/habitual facts) together.
examStrategy.marathi: Yes/No व WH Questions, Imperative व Negative Imperative, Exclamatory, Optative Sentences, Modal Changes आणि No-Tense-Change Exceptions (Universal Truth, Scientific/Historical/Habitual Facts) एकत्र revise करा.

goldenRevision: Present Reporting Verb -> No Tense Change
